name: Evidence of Equivalent Fraction Recognition
description: Evidence model for the claim that a student can recognize equivalent fractions represented in different forms.
claimStatement: The student can correctly identify fractions that are equivalent in value even when expressed with different numerators and denominators.

warrants.reasoningStatement: Correctly selecting the equivalent fraction from distractors requires recognizing that equivalent fractions represent the same point on the number line.
warrants.performanceCondition: Presented with a target fraction and four answer options, no calculator allowed.
warrants.limitationClause: Does not by itself establish fluency with mixed numbers or fraction operations.

observables.statement: Student selects the fraction equivalent to the target fraction from a set of distractors.
observables.boundaryNote: Distractors include common error patterns (e.g., doubling only the numerator).

evidenceRule.activationCondition: Correct option selected on first attempt.
evidenceRule.justification: A correct first-attempt selection is strong evidence of equivalence understanding rather than guessing.

decisionRule.justification: Threshold set from prior calibration study on the Grade 6 fractions item pool.

name: Evidence of Fraction Comparison
description: Evidence model for the claim that a student can compare the relative size of two fractions.
claimStatement: The student can correctly determine which of two fractions represents a greater quantity.

warrants.reasoningStatement: Correctly ordering two fractions with unlike denominators requires converting to a common reference (common denominator or decimal equivalent).
warrants.performanceCondition: Presented with two fractions with unlike denominators, no calculator allowed.
warrants.limitationClause: Does not establish understanding of fraction equivalence in isolation.

observables.statement: Student correctly selects the larger of two given fractions.
observables.boundaryNote: Fraction pairs are selected to avoid same-numerator or same-denominator shortcuts.

evidenceRule.activationCondition: Correct option selected on first attempt.
evidenceRule.justification: Correct comparison under these constraints indicates genuine magnitude reasoning.

decisionRule.justification: Threshold aligned with the equivalent-fractions evidence model for consistency across the construct.
